back: A word placed before a noun to show which one, whose, or how many/how much.
notes: Articles (a, an, the), demonstratives (this, those), possessives (my, their), quantifiers (some, many, few, each).

back: Decided by the first SOUND: an hour, an honest man, an MBA; a university, a European, a one-way street.
For something already mentioned or known to both speaker and listener, for unique things (the sun), and with rivers, oceans, mountain ranges and plural country names.
notes: the Zambezi, the Indian Ocean, the United Kingdom.

back: With plural and uncountable nouns used generally (Water is essential), with most countries, towns, single lakes and mountains, and with meals and sports.
notes: Zimbabwe, Mutare, Lake Kariba, Mount Nyangani; we had lunch; they play football.

back: much + uncountable (much water); many + plural countable (many pupils).
notes: In positive statements, a lot of is more natural than much.

front: Few / a few, little / a little
back: a few / a little = some (positive); few / little = hardly any (negative). Few goes with countable nouns, little with uncountable.
notes: I have a few friends (good). There was little hope (bad).

back: fewer + plural countable nouns (fewer people); less + uncountable nouns (less rain).
All take a singular noun and singular verb. Each can refer to two; every needs three or more and is never followed by of.
notes: Neither road leads there. Each of the two boys has a bag.

back: some in positive statements and offers; any in negatives and most questions.
notes: We saw some lions. We did not see any elephants. Would you like some tea?
